summary: Douglas County lookout near Elkton, Oregon: 1928 spar-tree platform, steel tower from 1942-43, cut to 105 ft in 1963, removed by 1978.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1965, sold for salvage and removed by 1978; a 1980 survey description mentions only survey marks at the site

staffing.status: J.L. Rowe lookout 1939-1942; not staffed in 1963; discontinued after the 1965 fire season

events.note: Douglas fire patrol station in the tops of two Douglas fir spar trees, with a platform 114 or 117 feet up
J.B. Fullerton manned the station, per a July 1928 item
J.L. Rowe taken off the lookout for the summer
Steel from a 125-foot Richfield beacon built into a three-legged lookout tower; newspapers have it in use by August 1942; register dates the steel tower to 1943
J.L. Rowe held the lookout job in the 1942 season; an elevator was built for the lookout
Columbus Day storm damaged the tower
Rebuilt at 105 feet with a new cab and stairs in place of the elevator; not staffed in 1963
Register says abandoned in 1965; lookout discontinued after the fire season
Tower sold for salvage and removed; cabin moved to the Coos Bay area as a fishing cabin
National Geodetic Survey described the survey marks at the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and newspapers date the original two-tree station to 1928. A 1941 Douglas FPA annual report, quoted on a history page, says 1927. The story gives 1928 and notes the 1927 claim.

The register dates the 128-foot steel tower to 1943. Period items from May and August 1942 (The Forest Log, The Eugene Guard) describe the steel being built and in use in 1942. The story reports both.
One 1942 item places the Richfield beacon north of Roseburg and another near Winchester. Both are reported in the story.
Two 1928 items (The Timberman, September; The Sunday Oregonian, July) give the platform height as 114 feet and 117 feet. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 36.6 (120 ft) matches no height in the pages read: the register gives 128 ft for the 1943 steel tower, the history page gives 130 ft for the 1942 tower, and 105 ft after the 1963 rebuild. The record's source for 36.6 should be checked. The brief's 2010 FFLOS registration date (November 22, 2010) does not appear in the register text read, so it is not repeated. The Tillamook County Bell Mountain (FFLOS US 669) is a different site and was excluded. A Douglas Forest Protective Association Facebook post seen in search says the 1962 storm destroyed the tower; it was not read, and the register and history page say damaged, which the story follows. Current access and land ownership are not described in any source read, so access is omitted.
